suread: review R1 素读（只读 text/，未开 md）

facts.fact: 章首她仍保留灵异解释的可能：一部分的她怀疑是超自然物毁了 Leon 的速写本
facts.anchor: part of me wondered whether something otherworldly had destroyed Uncle Leon’s sketchbook

facts.fact: 她给出的灵异理由是：溜进浴室那个形状快得不像人
facts.anchor: the shape I’d seen slipping into the bathroom had been too quick to be a person

facts.fact: 她承接既有信念：农场之上悬着某种恶性，可能源自神话鳄鱼的诅咒
facts.anchor: some kind of malevolence hung over the farm, possibly stemming from a mythical alligator’s curse

facts.fact: 她据此反问：Ida Greer 在屋里的 haint 为什么不能也是真的
facts.anchor: why couldn’t Ida Greer’s haint in the house be real, too?

facts.fact: 反问的第二层：为什么它不能有实体显现
facts.anchor: Why couldn’t it manifest physically?

facts.fact: 她自己给灵异路线泼冷水：想不到 Ida 为什么要费事管一本旧速写本
facts.anchor: I couldn’t come up with a reason for Ida to bother with an old sketchbook

facts.fact: 她拍板：作案的必须是真人
facts.anchor: The culprit had to be a real person

facts.fact: 她限定嫌疑人范围：能进她房间的三个人里，只有一个在 Leon 日记里被负面写过
facts.anchor: only one of the three people with access to my room had featured negatively in Uncle Leon’s journal

facts.fact: 时间锚：那个周六下午
facts.anchor: That Saturday afternoon

facts.fact: 她把自己在温室里扎下来，观察院子
facts.anchor: I parked myself in the conservatory, where I studied the yard

facts.fact: 院子一夜之间向房子逼近三尺
facts.anchor: which had grown three feet closer to the house overnight

facts.fact: 她的条件句：若非先前见过那条边界，她可能根本不知道它存在过
facts.anchor: If I hadn’t seen the border before, I may not have known it ever existed

facts.fact: 草像爪子一样伸向玻璃墙
facts.anchor: Grass reached toward the glass walls like claws

facts.fact: 她把这与农场不断生长的藻类和漏水并置
facts.anchor: Just like the ever-growing algae and leaks at the farm

facts.fact: 她把逼近归因给 Ironheart 的可能：是它在悄悄扩张领地吗
facts.anchor: Was this Ironheart, stealthily expanding its territory?

facts.fact: Gazzie 的声音：好了，我们出发
facts.anchor: “All right,” Gazzie said, “let’s head out.”

facts.fact: Gazzie 的声音让她一抖
facts.anchor: Her voice made me jump

facts.fact: 她定神后打量 Gazzie 的脸
facts.anchor: Composing myself, I scanned her face

facts.fact: 她心里问的是：Gazzie 半夜进过我房间吗
facts.anchor: Had she entered my room in the middle of the night?

facts.fact: 她给这个问题一个「也许」
facts.anchor: Had she entered my room in the middle of the night? Maybe.

facts.fact: 第二问：我问了会不会冒犯她；答：肯定会
facts.anchor: Would she be offended if I asked? Definitely.

facts.fact: 她问去哪
facts.anchor: “Where to?” I asked

facts.fact: Gazzie 不肯说，路上再说；人已退回厨房
facts.anchor: “Tell you on the way,” she said, already disappearing back into the kitchen

facts.fact: 停车场里 Gazzie 的 SUV 与空调、蝉鸣和声
facts.anchor: Gazzie’s SUV hummed in harmony with the AC and cicadas

facts.fact: 转过 Greer House 的街角，她整个人松弛下来
facts.anchor: When we turned the corner from Greer House, my entire body sagged with relief

facts.fact: 她的感受：像在把某物—某人—留在屋里
facts.anchor: I felt like we were leaving something—someone—inside

facts.fact: Gazzie 问：你去过烤整猪吗
facts.anchor: “You ever been to a hog roast?” Gazzie asked

facts.fact: 她没去过，并如此说明
facts.anchor: I hadn’t, explaining as much

facts.fact: 是 Ginny 的女朋友要办
facts.anchor: “Ginny’s girlfriend’s having one.”

facts.fact: 叙述者确认名字：Henri
facts.anchor: “Henri?”

facts.fact: 她们只去过 Henri 的烘焙坊一次
facts.anchor: Though we’d visited her bakery once

facts.fact: 那次 Henri 本人不在，出门送婚礼蛋糕了
facts.anchor: the woman herself had been out delivering a wedding cake

facts.fact: Aunt Virginia 也不常在，没能多讲她
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia hadn’t been around enough to tell me much more about her

facts.fact: 她开始通过great-aunt留下的东西察觉她的缺席
facts.anchor: I’d begun to notice my great-aunt’s absence through what she left behind

facts.fact: 留下的具体物：厨房台面上的水煮蛋和麦片、便当上的便利贴
facts.anchor: boiled eggs and cereal on the kitchen counter, sticky notes on our packed lunches

facts.fact: Gazzie 判 Henri 只是客气
facts.anchor: “Henri’s being polite,” Gazzie said.

facts.fact: Gazzie 自陈：Henri 不喜欢我
facts.anchor: Inviting us. She doesn’t care for me.

facts.fact: 叙述者给退路：想去别处我也乐意
facts.anchor: “If you’d rather go somewhere else, I’d be happy to.”

facts.fact: 她的盘算：派对是跟 Gazzie 拉近关系的绝佳机会
facts.anchor: A party would be the perfect opportunity to schmooze with Gazzie

facts.fact: 但如果她更想一对一，她也接受
facts.anchor: but if she was more comfortable one-on-one, I’d take that, too

facts.fact: 她还想找机会问速写本
facts.anchor: I could even find an opening to ask her about the sketchbook

facts.fact: 她猜想 Gazzie 可能不知道她发现的那层架
facts.anchor: Maybe she didn’t know about the shelf I’d found

facts.fact: Gazzie 说 Ginny 一直催她社交
facts.anchor: “Ginny’s been onto me about being social.

facts.fact: Gazzie 说要让自己别去想农场那摊事
facts.anchor: I need to get my mind off the mess at the farm.

facts.fact: Gazzie 的三合一理由：正吃晚饭，烤猪一石三鸟
facts.anchor: It’s dinnertime. Hog roast kills all three birds.”

facts.fact: 她把收音机切到古典频道并满意地哼了一声
facts.anchor: She flipped the radio to a classical music channel and grunted with satisfaction

facts.fact: 她的自评：那一晚上的贴心长谈就这么没了
facts.anchor: There went our evening-long heart-to-heart.

facts.fact: 她随即又打起精神：还没全丢
facts.anchor: But all wasn’t lost, I realized, perking up

facts.fact: 理由：在车里她仍能试探 Gazzie 是否进过她房间
facts.anchor: while we were in the car, I could still feel out whether she’d been in my room

facts.fact: 她开口问：知不知道 Leon 留下过速写本
facts.anchor: “Do you know if Uncle Leon left any sketchbooks lying around?

facts.fact: Gazzie 的反应是握紧方向盘、指节发白
facts.anchor: Her hands gripped the steering wheel, knuckles whitening.

facts.fact: Gazzie 答：大概有；Ginny 才知道在哪儿
facts.anchor: “Probably. Ginny would know where they are.

facts.fact: Gazzie 把收音机拧大，示意谈话结束
facts.anchor: Turning up the radio, Gazzie signaled the end of our chat

facts.fact: 叙述者的读法：她承认了速写本可能存在，但不愿谈
facts.anchor: She’d admitted to the sketchbooks’ potential existence but seemed reluctant to discuss them

facts.fact: 她的不解：为何对一些旧画感到不自在
facts.anchor: Why feel uncomfortable about some old drawings?

facts.fact: 她没得到答案，只添了一层说不出口new fear：Gazzie 仍在瞒她
facts.anchor: only a new, unarticulated fear that she was still hiding something from me

facts.fact: Henri 住在 Amelia Island 东侧
facts.anchor: Henri lived on Amelia Island’s east side

facts.fact: 离 Greer House 近，但近不到傍晚暑气里能走过去
facts.anchor: close to Greer House but not close enough to walk in the late-afternoon heat

facts.fact: Henri 的房子窄，往高三层
facts.anchor: Her narrow house stretched three stories tall

facts.fact: 玻璃墙在褪去的日光里发亮，前门是暗色流线金属
facts.anchor: Glass walls glimmered in the fading sunlight, and the front door was a dark, sleek metal

facts.fact: 进门后宾客握着细长杯柄的杯子
facts.anchor: Inside, partygoers grasped delicate long-stemmed glasses

facts.fact: 许多人头发花白
facts.anchor: Many sported gray and white hair

facts.fact: 空中是酒与汗的气味
facts.anchor: The smell of wine sweat hung in the air

facts.fact: 她们进来时几个客人看一眼，多数挥手点头后又继续聊天
facts.anchor: Several guests glanced over when we walked in, most waving, inclining their heads, then resuming their conversations

facts.fact: 包括没正式致意的在内，所有人都对 Gazzie 的存在有反应
facts.anchor: Everyone, including those who didn’t acknowledge Gazzie formally, responded to her presence

facts.fact: 她经过时众人挺直背、笑得更响、眼睛滑向她
facts.anchor: As she passed, they straightened their backs and laughed louder, their eyes sliding to her

facts.fact: 她分辨不出：这些人是想讨好她还是怕她
facts.anchor: I couldn’t tell whether they wanted to impress her or were afraid of her

facts.fact: 她的下一句：他们对她 certainly 有看法，不论哪一头
facts.anchor: They certainly had opinions about her, one way or another.

facts.fact: 她给出的历史根：Ida 一杀掉传奇鳄鱼就在镇上臭名远播
facts.anchor: Ida Greer had been infamous in the town as soon as she’d killed the legendary alligator

facts.fact: 更甚的是她——一个女人！从前的女仆——创办捕鳄生意、再办农场
facts.anchor: even more so when she—a woman! a former lady’s maid!—started an alligator hunting business, then the farm

facts.fact: 一百年来镇上人或听说过、或编造过关于富有而偏执的 Greer 家的故事
facts.anchor: surely locals had heard or started stories about the rich, obsessive Greers in their house filled with portraits

facts.fact: 故事的题材：死去的丈夫、诅咒、haints
facts.anchor: about dead husbands and curses and haints

facts.fact: Gazzie 不理他们，直奔屋后
facts.anchor: Gazzie ignored them, beelining for the back of the house

facts.fact: 她们找到 Aunt Virginia 倚在大理石中岛台边
facts.anchor: We found Aunt Virginia leaning on a marble kitchen island

facts.fact: 那位高个黑人女性编着 box braids，一只手臂轻轻环着 Virginia
facts.anchor: A tall Black woman with box braids wrapped one arm lightly around her

facts.fact: Virginia 的脸朝她仰上去并笑
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia’s face tilted up toward the woman, and she laughed

facts.fact: 叙述者看得出神，对速写本的焦虑被冲走
facts.anchor: I studied them, rapt, my anxiety about Uncle Leon’s sketchbooks washing away

facts.fact: 她的原话：我从没见过两个如此显然相爱的人
facts.anchor: I’d never known two people so obviously in love

facts.fact: 她的羡慕：那样属于一个人一定很妙；有一个人属于你
facts.anchor: It must feel wonderful to belong to someone like that. To have someone belong to you.

facts.fact: Virginia 一看到 Gazzie，笑容掉了一点点又按回去
facts.anchor: When Aunt Virginia spotted Gazzie, her smile fell a fraction, but she pulled it back in place

facts.fact: Virginia 热络地说：你们来了；我还担心周六游客把岛堵满
facts.anchor: “I was worried about the traffic—tourists flood the island on Saturdays.

facts.fact: Virginia 把手放在高个女性的腹部，介绍：Dart，这是 Henri
facts.anchor: Placing her hand on the tall woman’s stomach, she said, “Dart, this is Henri.”

facts.fact: Henri 伸手自我介绍：全名 Henrietta，但大家都说 Henri 更配她
facts.anchor: Henri stuck out her hand. “Henrietta, but I’ve heard Henri suits me better.

facts.fact: 叙述者认同：Henrietta 让人想到牛仔靴和嚼烟
facts.anchor: It did. Henrietta brought to mind cowboy boots and chewing tobacco.

facts.fact: Henri 穿无袖丝亮黄上衣、宽松黑长裤
facts.anchor: In contrast, Henri wore a sleeveless, silky yellow top and loose black trousers

facts.fact: 上衣与 Virginia 发上的黄丝带同色；叙述者喜欢「她们是故意配」这个念头
facts.anchor: Her top matched the yellow ribbon in Aunt Virginia’s hair. I loved the idea of them matching on purpose.

facts.fact: 叙述者说很高兴认识你
facts.anchor: “Nice to meet you,” I said

facts.fact: Henri 用另一只手盖住她握着的手
facts.anchor: “Likewise,” she said, covering my clasped hand with her free one.

facts.fact: Henri 轻轻握了一下才放开，并说久仰
facts.anchor: “I’ve heard a lot about you.

facts.fact: 叙述者不知怎么接
facts.anchor: I smiled, unsure how to respond.

facts.fact: 她的据：以她所知 Mama 从没跟任何人提起过她，哪怕在有工作有同事的时候
facts.anchor: To my knowledge, Mama hadn’t ever talked about me to anyone, not even when she had a job and coworkers

facts.fact: 她岔开话题：猪在烤炉里了吗
facts.anchor: “Is the hog in the oven?”

facts.fact: 三个女人都笑了，连 Gazzie 也笑
facts.anchor: All three women laughed, even Gazzie.

facts.fact: Virginia 解释：整猪塞不进烤箱，Henri 已经在外头架好了
facts.anchor: “Hog won’t fit in the oven,” Aunt Virginia explained. “Henri’s already set it up outside.”

facts.fact: Henri 说还得一会儿才好，而且守着火太热
facts.anchor: “It’ll be a bit before it’s ready,” Henri added, “and it’s too hot to stand by the fire.”

facts.fact: Gazzie 说我来看着
facts.anchor: “I’ll watch it,” Gazzie said

facts.fact: Henri 想婉拒：你太好了，可是——
facts.anchor: “That’s kind of you,” Henri began, “but—”

facts.fact: 三人看着 Gazzie 消失在人群里
facts.anchor: The three of us watched Gazzie disappear into the crowd

facts.fact: Virginia 带着歉意转向 Henri，Henri 重新环住她并轻轻摇头
facts.anchor: Henri slipped her arm around Virginia again, gently shaking her head

facts.fact: 叙述者移开视线，像在偷看一段私密对话
facts.anchor: I glanced away, feeling like I was interrupting a private conversation

facts.fact: Henri 给她倒了白葡萄酒；她明知不该喝——不想应付酒精引起的症状——还是喝了
facts.anchor: Henri poured me a glass of white wine, which I shouldn’t have taken—I didn’t want to deal with alcohol-induced symptoms—but did anyway

facts.fact: 她给自己立的限：只一口压惊
facts.anchor: I promised myself I wouldn’t have more than a sip to calm my nerves

facts.fact: 她承认诱惑在： blackout，把 Greer House 的谜一起忘掉
facts.anchor: even if the thought of blacking out, of forgetting about Greer House’s mysteries, was tempting

facts.fact: 客人在厨房穿行，拿魔鬼蛋、祝贺 Henri 的家漂亮
facts.anchor: Guests flowed through the kitchen, picking up deviled eggs, congratulating Henri on her beautiful home

facts.fact: 原文此处是残句：Virginia 的眼睛跟着 Henri 的一举一动
facts.anchor: As Aunt Virginia’s eyes followed Henri’s every move.

facts.fact: 叙述者：我从没见过她这么松弛、这么快乐
facts.anchor: I’d never seen her so relaxed. So happy.

facts.fact: 她的推论：难怪 Virginia 不怎么待在 Greer House——她大概一直和 Henri 在一起
facts.anchor: No wonder she hadn’t been spending much time at Greer House; she’d probably been with Henri all along

facts.fact: 天空转成粉色时 Henri 挥手让客人到外头
facts.anchor: When the sky turned pink, Henri waved her guests outside

facts.fact: 后院望得见一道沙丘，海浪在它之外轰鸣
facts.anchor: Her backyard overlooked a sand dune, waves roaring beyond it

facts.fact: 火上一整只猪，头和蹄都在，在铁扦上转，黑眼睛直直鼓着
facts.anchor: a whole hog, head and feet included, rotated on an iron spit, its black eyes bulging straight ahead

facts.fact: 猪的粉脸颊像是晒伤小孩的脸；叙述者移开眼
facts.anchor: Its pink cheeks might have belonged to a sunburned child. I averted my eyes.

facts.fact: 她想到 Savannah 那些素食同事吃鸡肉沙拉时的恶心感
facts.anchor: Had my vegan coworkers in Savannah felt this nauseated when I’d eaten chicken salad at lunch?

facts.fact: Gazzie 对这场「屠杀」无动于衷，一手摇 crank 一手端红葡萄酒
facts.anchor: Gazzie, unbothered by the carnage, worked the crank with one hand and held a glass of red wine in the other

facts.fact: 她脚边地上躺着一个空瓶
facts.anchor: An empty bottle lay on the ground beside her

facts.fact: 她旁边站着 Harrison，眼神相接时举起啤酒罐致意
facts.anchor: Next to her stood Harrison, who lifted his beer can in greeting when our eyes met

facts.fact: 她没想到会见到他，虽然本该知道他会在
facts.anchor: I hadn’t expected to see him, though I should have known he’d be there

facts.fact: 一个小男孩绕着他跑圈，他弯腰去抓，男孩笑得尖叫
facts.anchor: A little boy ran in a circle around him, and he leaned over to grab at him, making the boy squeal with laughter

facts.fact: 这个姿势让她想起他谈起父亲时的温情
facts.anchor: His gesture was warm and familiar, reminding me of the fond way he spoke of his father

facts.fact: 她的推论（带 probably，非原文事实）：童年幸福，他大概想要孩子
facts.anchor: Given his happy childhood, he probably wanted kids.

facts.fact: 毫无预警，她脑中重播 Harrison 的目光落到她唇上，脸颊发烫
facts.anchor: my mind replayed Harrison’s eyes falling to my lips, and, to my horror, my cheeks heated

facts.fact: 她的顾虑：若他发现她幻想过这种事，他会得意得受不了
facts.anchor: If he found out I’d imagined something like that, he’d be insufferably smug

facts.fact: Gazzie 举杯致意把她注意力redirect，像停机坪上的引导员
facts.anchor: Gazzie lifted her wineglass in a salute, redirecting my attention like a plane marshaller on the tarmac

facts.fact: Gazzie 问：你劈过柴吗
facts.anchor: “You ever chop wood?

facts.fact: 她说没有，但是——
facts.anchor: “No, but—”

facts.fact: Gazzie 口齿不清地模仿女童军接话：你愿意学
facts.anchor: “You’re willing to learn,” she slurred in a poor mimicry of a Girl Scout

facts.fact: Gazzie 说正需要劈柴的，并把 Harrison 叫上
facts.anchor: “Great, because we need some. Harrison?”

facts.fact: Gazzie 挥手让他们去侧院，Harrison 与她对视后耸肩
facts.anchor: As Gazzie waved us to the side yard, he caught my eye and shrugged

facts.fact: 走路时他双臂松松甩着；两人的手撞了一下，她猛地抽开
facts.anchor: Our hands bumped, and I jerked mine away

facts.fact: 她们停在两英尺高的木柴堆前；旁边树桩上插着一把斧，刃在光里发亮
facts.anchor: We stopped before a two-foot-tall pile of logs. Beside it was an axe stuck in a tree stump, its blade glinting in the light

facts.fact: 他闷哼一声搬起一根木头竖立在桩上，再握住斧柄把它从桩里拔出
facts.anchor: With a grunt, he picked up one log and placed it on the stump, balancing it vertically. Then he grabbed the axe handle and wrenched it out of the stump

facts.fact: 他说：我先劈一根，然后你劈一根
facts.anchor: “I’ll do one, then you’ll do one,” he said

facts.fact: 他把斧扛上肩，斧刃在空中摇晃
facts.anchor: He hoisted the axe onto his shoulder, and the blade wobbled in the air

facts.fact: 她打趣：你确定你能碰利器？
facts.anchor: “You sure you should be handling a sharp object?” I quipped

facts.fact: 他闷声回：看着就好
facts.anchor: “Just watch,” he grumbled

facts.fact: 路过的派对客怪叫一声，同伴大笑； Harrison 两人都没理会
facts.anchor: A partygoer walking by whooped, and his friend laughed. Harrison ignored them both

facts.fact: 他一心教我：全在摆荡的劲儿里
facts.anchor: “It’s all in the swing,” he continued, intent on instructing me

facts.fact: 他挥下把木头整齐劈成两半
facts.anchor: He swung and struck the log, which broke neatly in half

facts.fact: 她从没觉得劈柴美，但他动得又自信又有力
facts.anchor: I’d never considered cutting wood beautiful, but he moved with confidence and power

facts.fact: 她的短句结论：没有犹豫
facts.anchor: No hesitation.

facts.fact: 她的俏皮判定： apparently 他只在鳄鱼面前心软
facts.anchor: Apparently, he was only soft when it came to alligators

facts.fact: 他说「轮到你」，轻轻握住她前臂把她拉到他站的位置
facts.anchor: “Your turn.” He gently grasped my forearm and pulled me to his spot

facts.fact: 光滑的斧柄被他汗浸得发滑，几乎脱手；比她预期的重，搁上肩就乱晃
facts.anchor: The smooth axe handle, slick with his sweat, nearly slipped from my hand

facts.fact: 他放上另一根木头，把手掌压在彼女の手的上下方
facts.anchor: Harrison set another log on the stump, then placed his hands on the axe above and below mine

facts.fact: 她的体感：这个姿势几乎等于从背后抱住她；她酒喝够了，没有抗议
facts.anchor: Positioned like this, he was practically hugging me from behind. I’d had enough wine not to protest.

facts.fact: 他先说：先练挥，好吗？呼吸热在她颊上
facts.anchor: “Practice swings first, yeah?” he said, his breath hot on my cheek

facts.fact: 他们一起举斧，Harrison 在落到木头上之前停住这一挥
facts.anchor: We raised the axe together, Harrison stopping our swing just before it hit the wood

facts.fact: 他说：你得投入；我感得到你在犹豫
facts.anchor: “You’ve got to commit,” he said. “I can feel you hesitating.

facts.fact: 她的反驳（内心）：他在拖慢斧头的动量，她怎么用力挥？
facts.anchor: How was I supposed to swing hard when he was slowing down the axe’s momentum?

facts.fact: 她甩开他：我能自己来
facts.anchor: I shook him off. “I can do it.”

facts.fact: 他双手一举作投降状，退开
